annotations.text:
Four directions for the app panel, all on shadcn neutral tokens + Geist.

Pick a DIRECTION, not a detail — I'll build the chosen one out properly.
Each has a real tradeoff below it.

A · QUIET LIST
No cards at all. One white sheet, hairline rules, labels left / machine values right in mono.

Why: closest to shadcn defaults and to Cursor's sidebar rows. Calmest, reads fastest, ages best.
Tradeoff: least visual hierarchy — every row looks equally important, so nothing draws the eye when something breaks.

B · RAIL + DETAIL
Cursor's actual structure: a nav rail inside the drawer, content beside it. No push-navigation at all.

Why: every section is one click from every other, and detail screens get real room — the analytics view stops feeling cramped.
Tradeoff: needs ~860px, so it covers much more of the user's app. Least suited to a narrow overlay.

C · SHADCN CARDS
Literal shadcn Card: white cards, 1px border, 8px radius, on a muted ground. Two-up grid.

Why: nearest to what's shipped, so it's the smallest change — a retoken rather than a rebuild. Familiar to anyone who has used a shadcn app.
Tradeoff: the most generic of the four. It will look like every other dashboard built this year.

D · DENSE READOUT
Mono-forward key/value rows under uppercase group labels. Everything on one screen, no navigation.

Why: this is the one that actually nods to your repo's own 'blueprint' system in globals.css — squared, mono, green as the only hue. Fastest to answer 'is my app fine?'
Tradeoff: reads as a tool for engineers, not a product surface. Weakest for the non-technical owner.
